relevance_note: Single-patient letter describing a GFAP carrier with Alexander disease: "GFAP) sequencing analysis revealed a novel heterozygous missense mutation (c.1087A>G)".
method_note: Hand-extracted from the text and the Fig. 1 legend (no tables in the paper); JSON assembled with a short script. Parents included as tested-negative relatives ('her asymptomatic parents'); sex not stated, so labelled 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2'; 'asymptomatic' was not turned into feature rows or checklist exclusions because it names no specific feature. Inheritance recorded as de novo because the variant 'was not found ... in her asymptomatic parents' (both parents tested, absent), although the paper never uses the words 'de novo'. Transcript left 'not reported': NM_002055.4 appears only as the GenBank accession for the Homo sapiens ortholog in the conservation panel (Fig. 1L), not as the HGVS reference. Pathogenicity: authors call it a 'novel ... mutation'; PolyPhen-2 'probably damaging' is a tool prediction and is not recorded as the authors' classification; no functional assay reported. Age at onset left 'not reported': febrile seizure at 3 years is recorded as a feature onset, and gait/urinary symptoms are given only as 'a 5-year history' at age 16 (no age stated); the title calls it late-onset. 'No bulbar signs' was not used to exclude dysphagia or dysarthria (examination signs vs symptoms; narrow/broad rule). Periventricular rim left 'not reported': the paper mentions a DRP 'within the periventricular rim' only for two previously published juvenile patients (ref 3), and describes this patient's lesions as periventricular WM/area. Those two previously published patients (ref 3) were given no rows: mentioned only as a pair with no individual-level detail. No contradictions found.
